__doc: THE ATTRIBUTE TREE. 7 categories, 29 sub-stats, every one rated 1-100. Category scores are a WEIGHTED AVERAGE of their sub-stats and exist ONLY for display - the match engine always reads individual sub-stats. Everything in this file is safe to tune: change a weight, save, and the app hot-reloads.
__count_note: The design brief said 26 sub-stats but then listed 29 of them. The list won, so there are 29. To drop three, delete them from a category's `subs` array AND from every player in real_players.json.

displayCalibration.__doc: Final tweak applied to the single OVR number only: ovr = weightedCategoryAverage * scale + offset. It exists so the OVR shown under a real player lands close to the value written in real_players.json. Set scale 1 / offset 0 to see the raw maths.

displayBands.__doc: COLOUR BANDS for the sub-stat and category numbers on the PLAYER PROFILE - the Attributes tab, the radar chart and its legend. Top band first; `from` is the lowest value that still counts as that band, and `hex` is the colour it is drawn in. Only the profile uses these, so changing them cannot make a tournament lobby rating turn red.
displayBands.__scale_note: These are ELITE-ROSTER bands, straight from the design brief: at the top of the world an 80 really is a weakness. That means a freshly generated academy player will look almost entirely red, because next to Peterbot they are. If you would rather see shades of progress on your own young roster, add bands underneath, for example a Developing band from 65 and a Raw band from 0, and change the last band below to start at 72.

radar.__doc: The seven-sided radar chart at the top of the ATTRIBUTES tab. It plots the seven CATEGORY scores, which are display-only rollups of the sub-stats - the match engine never reads them.
radar.__min: The value at the centre of the web. Anything at or below this sits ON the centre point, so set it below the worst category you expect to look at - a rookie can have an Offspawn of 45, and at min 60 that category would vanish. Raise it toward 80 ONLY if you are comparing world-top players to each other, where everything sits between 78 and 96 and a radar drawn from 0 shows seven near-identical blobs.
radar.__max: The value at the outer ring.
radar.__rings: How many guide rings are drawn between min and max.

categoryWeights.__doc: How much each CATEGORY counts toward the single OVR number. Only the ratios matter - they get normalised. Raising `fighting` makes fighters look better on paper; it does NOT change how the match engine behaves (that is balance.json).

categories.name: Aim
categories.blurb: Raw shooting. What the crosshair does before anything else is considered.

subs.name: Tracking
subs.desc: Holding the crosshair on a moving target - sprays, ARs, close-range SMG duels.

subs.name: Flicks
subs.desc: Snapping onto a target that just appeared. Shotgun and sniper timing.

subs.name: Accuracy
subs.desc: Overall hit rate. How much of the magazine actually lands.

subs.name: Headshot Aim
subs.desc: Finding heads under pressure. Turns a two-shot into a one-shot.

categories.name: Mechanics
categories.blurb: Raw building and editing speed. Hands, not decisions.

subs.name: Build Speed
subs.desc: Getting the wall, ramp and cone up before the shot lands.

subs.name: Build Efficiency
subs.desc: Doing it without burning 400 mats. Directly extends how long they last in an endgame.

subs.name: Edit Speed
subs.desc: How fast an edit goes through, confirmed and reset.

subs.name: Edit Accuracy
subs.desc: Hitting the edit they meant to hit. Misedits under pressure get people killed.

categories.name: Fighting
categories.blurb: How much raw ability actually CONVERTS in a real fight. In the sim this is a MULTIPLIER on Aim and Mechanics, not another additive stat.

subs.name: Edit IQ
subs.desc: Choosing the RIGHT edit, reading the shape of the opponent build.

subs.name: Piece Control
subs.desc: Taking and holding opponent pieces instead of trading them straight back.

subs.name: Box Fighting
subs.desc: Close-quarters box exchanges. The most common way a fight is actually decided.

subs.name: HG Retakes
subs.desc: Retaking high ground once it has been lost.

subs.name: Reset Timing
subs.desc: Knowing when to disengage instead of committing. The difference between cracked and good.

subs.name: Movement
subs.desc: Mantles, resets and repositioning mid-fight.

categories.name: Game Sense
categories.blurb: Everything decided on the map rather than inside a box.

subs.name: Positioning
subs.desc: Where they sit in zone, and how exposed that spot is to a third party.

subs.name: Rotation
subs.desc: Route quality AND how much damage they take getting there.

subs.name: Fight Selection
subs.desc: Picking mid-game fights they will actually win. Gates whether a fight even happens.

subs.name: Resource Mgmt
subs.desc: Mat and heal budgeting. Running dry in zone 8 is usually fatal.

categories.name: Offspawn
categories.blurb: The first ninety seconds. Bad loot caps how much everything else matters.

subs.name: Drop Accuracy
subs.desc: Drop quality and raw speed to the ground.

subs.name: Fifty-Fifties
subs.desc: Winning a contested chest race for the first gun.

subs.name: Offspawn Fights
subs.desc: Fighting with bad loot, or none at all.

categories.name: Mental
categories.blurb: The head. Half of this category only shows up once something has already gone wrong.

subs.name: Clutch
subs.desc: 1v2s and 1v3s. Only checked when they are actually the last one alive.

subs.name: Under Pressure
subs.desc: Last game of a session, got landed on, must-win situations.

subs.name: Tilt Resistance
subs.desc: Bouncing back after a disaster match. Applies to the match AFTER the bad one.

subs.name: Big Stage Nerve
subs.desc: LAN and Grand Finals ONLY - completely ignored at every other event. GROWS with LAN appearances: a young player with no LAN record starts low and has to earn it.

subs.name: Consistency
subs.desc: Controls the SIZE of their random variance roll. Low = boom or bust. It is not a quality rating.

categories.name: Teamwork
categories.blurb: What they add to the players sitting next to them.

subs.name: Communication
subs.desc: Callout quality. Lifts the whole duo.

subs.name: Decision Making
subs.desc: Drives the team rotations and calls. The IGL stat.

subs.name: Adaptivity
subs.desc: How fast they gel with a new partner. Controls the synergy ramp.

peakModel.__doc: PEAK is every player's hidden ceiling, stored per sub-stat exactly like CURRENT. Generated players get peak = current + a gap. Peak is never shown as a number for an unsigned player.

gapByAge.__doc: Base gap (mu) and spread (sigma) in rating points, by age. Ages in between are interpolated. A 14-year-old has a lot of room left; a 24-year-old has none.

categoryGapScale.__doc: Multiplier on that gap, per category. Hands (aim, mechanics) are nearly finished early - a 17-year-old is already close to their mechanical ceiling. Heads (game sense, mental, teamwork) keep growing for years, which is why veterans stay relevant.

peakModel.__ceiling: No peak value may ever exceed this.

bigStageNerve.__doc: THE HEADLINE PROGRESSION MECHANIC. Big Stage Nerve is the one sub-stat a player cannot train - it is earned by turning up to LANs and Grand Finals. Read by the progression code in players.ts.

startByAge.__doc: Where a freshly generated player's CURRENT Big Stage Nerve sits before they have played a single LAN. Interpolated between the listed ages. Deliberately brutal for kids - this is why the 17-year-old world #1 loses the Grand Final.

bigStageNerve.__startSigma: Random spread on that starting value.

peakBonusByAge.__doc: Added to `startByAge` to give the AGE-ANCHORED CEILING for Big Stage Nerve. A player can never be given a nerve ceiling below what they have already earned, so a 20-year-old veteran who is already on 96 simply stays there - they have been to every LAN there is. All the headroom sits with the kids: a 15-year-old tops out around 91, a 17-year-old around 93, while their starting values are 64 and 72. That gap is the single biggest source of hidden upside on a young signing.

bigStageNerve.__peakResidual: Tiny extra ceiling for a player who has already earned past their age-anchored ceiling, so they are never completely frozen.
bigStageNerve.__gainPerLan: Points of Big Stage Nerve gained per LAN / Grand Final appearance, before the modifiers below. Raise this to make players harden faster.
bigStageNerve.__gainDecayPerLan: Each LAN is worth this fraction of the previous one, so the first LAN teaches far more than the twentieth. Set to 1.0 for flat linear growth.
bigStageNerve.__goodResultMultiplier: Applied when they finish in the top third of a LAN. Winning on stage teaches more than getting rolled on stage.
bigStageNerve.__badResultMultiplier: Applied when they finish in the bottom third. They still learn something, just not much.
bigStageNerve.__cannotBeTrained: If true, no training program may move Big Stage Nerve. Leave this on - the entire point is that it has to be earned at events.

decline.__doc: What happens after the decline age (progression.declineStartAge in balance.json, currently 22). Raw speed goes first; reads and mental keep climbing toward peak. Kami in real_players.json is the calibration case.
decline.__categoryDeclineScale: Multiplier on the weekly decline rate. NEGATIVE means the category still GROWS after the decline age - a 24-year-old's game sense and mental are still improving while their hands fall off.

legacyBridge.__doc: TEMPORARY SCAFFOLDING. Maps the 11 old attribute names onto groups of new sub-stats so the old match engine and the old training programs keep working while the sim is rewritten (build step 3) and training is rewired (build step 6). DELETE THIS BLOCK once both are done. Nothing the player sees depends on it.
